title: The number check accepts any figure from earlier turns and saved memories, so an invented count is shown as checked
evidence: $guardFacts = ['facts' => $facts, 'history' => array_column($history, 'content'), 'question' => $question];  ($facts also holds 'memories' => $memories). GuardsGeneratedText::numericValues() reads every digit run in those strings, including the list markers of earlier answers, which the guard strips only from the text being checked. Run against the current code on an in-memory database: (1) turn 1, the model answers with a list numbered 1 to 7; turn 2 'how many members still owe fees?', the model writes 'Exactly 7 members still owe fees.' -> stored with engine=claude, model_written=true, notice=null and the step 'Checked every number in the answer against those records'. The same sentence in a new conversation is rejected and replaced. (2) A memory 'the old treasurer mentioned 55,555.55' lets 'Your balance is PHP 55,555.55.' through in every later conversation. (3) Live on :8002: after a turn that mentions 987,654.32 and 4321, the stand-in's 'PHP 987,654.32 was spent on 4321 items.' is stored as a model-written answer.
impact: The fixed product rule is that a number that is not in the supplied facts is never shown. In any conversation longer than one turn the rule stops holding: every number in the last 8 messages (old answers about other records, ordered-list numbering, anything the user typed) and every number in up to 30 memories is treated as a fact for the current answer. A treasurer or the SAO can be shown a wrong count or amount with the reasoning line saying it was checked against the records. No hostile input is needed; an earlier numbered list is enough.
fix: Check each line against the facts built for this question only. In answerFromRecords() build the guard set as $guardFacts = ['facts' => Arr::except($facts, ['memories'])]; ($facts already carries the current question, so figures the person has just typed can still be repeated) and drop the 'history' and separate 'question' keys. The same set is used for reasoningLine(). Change contract 6.4 from 'against the facts, the conversation text, the memories and the question' to 'against the facts for this question and the question itself'. Add three tests to AskAiChatTest: a number that appears only in an earlier assistant turn, only in an earlier user turn, and only in a memory must each produce the replace event and model_written=false.

title: Any message of five words or fewer is answered with the previous answer's records, whatever it asks
evidence: looksLikeFollowUp(): if ($count <= 5) { return true; }  and resolveIntent() line 601 takes only the single latest assistant message: $previous = ...->where('role', 'assistant')->where('id', '<', $userMessage->id)->orderByDesc('id')->first(); a greeting, thanks or memory answer there ends the reuse. Live on :8000 (records only) as Admin 900001, after 'How is our budget doing this semester': 'who is the adviser?' -> intent finance_health, the budget summary again; 'ok thanks' and 'great' -> the budget summary a third and fourth time; after 'What should I do today?', 'who are the officers' -> the daily plan again. Against the current code on an in-memory database 'list all officers' after a finance answer also returns the budget summary. In a new conversation 'who is the adviser?' is answered correctly from the record search ('Found 16 matching record(s) ... Organization Adviser'). After 'thanks', 'tell me more' (live) and 'why?' (in-memory run) fall to a generic search because the latest assistant message is the thanks reply.
impact: Most chat messages are short. Once a conversation has one answer, every short question the keyword classifier does not recognise is answered with the wrong records: the person asks who the adviser is and gets budget figures, with no hint that the question was not understood. With a model the facts sent are the finance facts, so the model cannot answer either. Acknowledgements such as 'ok thanks' repeat the whole previous answer and cost a model call. The existing test (test_a_new_subject_is_not_forced_onto_the_previous_intent, line 209) only uses a subject the classifier knows, so it passes.
fix: Both the contract (6.1 says 'short, or leans on ...') and the code should change: shortness alone must not trigger reuse. (1) In looksLikeFollowUp() delete the '$count <= 5' branch and require a leaning word for up to 12 words: /\b(?:that|those|it|its|them|they|this|these|more|why|explain|elaborate|what about|how about|same|again|else|instead)\b|^(?:and|but|so|also)\b/iu. (2) In localAnswer() answer acknowledgements locally with greetingAnswer($user, true): /^(?:ok(?:ay)?|great|nice|cool|good|got it|i see|noted|alright|sige)?[\s,!.]*(?:thanks?|thank you|salamat|ty|thx)?[\s!.]*$/iu when the message is not empty. (3) In resolveIntent() look back to the latest assistant message whose payload.intent is not in LOCAL_INTENTS (add ->get() over the last few and take the first that qualifies) so a thanks in between does not drop the subject. Tests: after a finance answer 'who is the adviser?' and 'list all officers' give semantic_rag; 'ok thanks' gives greeting; 'thanks' then 'why?' gives finance_health.

title: Memory and 'what can you do' commands are matched as substrings: an ordinary question can wipe the memory or be answered with the capabilities list
evidence: Line 214: if (Str::contains($lower, ['forget everything', 'forget all', 'clear your memory', ...])) { ... AiMemory::ownedBy($user)->delete(); }  Line 234: Str::contains($lower, ['what can you do', 'what do you do', ..., 'who are you'])  Line 209: preg_match('/^(?:(?:please|pls|hey)[\s,]+)?remember\b(?:\s+that\b)?\s*[:\-,]?\s*(?<content>.+)$/isu'). Run against the current code: 'How do I make officers not forget all their tasks?' -> 'Done. I have forgotten everything you asked me to keep in mind.' and the memories are gone; 'remember that event last week?' -> 'Saved to memory: event last week?'; 'Remember when the fee was due?' -> saved; 'what can you do about unpaid fees?', 'What do you do when a member has not paid?' and 'who are you voting for?' -> the capabilities answer; 'what do you remember about the budget hearing?' -> the memory list.
impact: A typed question that happens to contain 'forget all' or 'clear memory' deletes up to 30 saved memories with no confirmation and no undo. Questions that begin with 'remember' are stored as junk memories, which are then sent to the model on every later question. Real questions about fees, voting or procedures get the generic capabilities text instead of an answer.
fix: Match whole messages, not substrings. Forget: /^(?:please\s+)?(?:forget\s+(?:everything|it\s+all|all\s+(?:of\s+)?(?:it|that|your\s+memor(?:y|ies)))|(?:clear|delete|erase|wipe)\s+(?:all\s+)?(?:your|my)?\s*memor(?:y|ies))[\s.!]*$/iu. List: /^(?:what\s+do\s+you\s+(?:currently\s+)?remember|what\s+have\s+you\s+remembered|what(?:'s|\s+is)\s+in\s+your\s+memory|(?:show|list)(?:\s+me)?\s+(?:your\s+|my\s+)?memor(?:y|ies)|what\s+are\s+my\s+memories)(?:\s+about\s+me)?[\s?.!]*$/iu. Capabilities: /^(?:(?:hi|hello|hey)[\s,!]+)?(?:what\s+can\s+you\s+do|what\s+do\s+you\s+do|what\s+can\s+i\s+ask(?:\s+you)?|how\s+can\s+you\s+help(?:\s+me)?|what\s+can\s+you\s+help(?:\s+me)?\s+with|what\s+are\s+you\s+able\s+to\s+do|what\s+are\s+your\s+capabilities|who\s+are\s+you)(?:\s+for\s+me)?[\s?.!]*$/iu. Remember: skip the save when the captured content ends with '?' or starts with when|what|who|where|why|how|if|the time\b, and let the message go to the normal answer. Add a test with each of the seven sentences above.

title: A stop or a dropped connection is noticed only when the server next writes, and it writes nothing while the model thinks or is inside a long line
evidence: The only check is at the start of each model event: if ($aborted !== null && $aborted()) { $stopped = true; throw new ChatInterrupted('client_left'); } where $aborted is connection_aborted() === 1 (AskAiController line 111). PHP sets that flag only when a write to the client fails. The reasoning branch (line 374) buffers until a newline and writes nothing; text is written only when a line completes; the loop at line 395 releases every buffered line without re-checking. Meanwhile the request holds Cache::lock('ask-ai-chat:'.$user->school_id, 150) (controller line 82). Live on :8002: aborted a stream after 0.9 s, sent a new message at once -> 429 {"message":"Wait for the current answer to finish."}; a second request sent straight after that -> the same 429; the lock was free about half a second later, which is one line of the fast stand-in model.
impact: After pressing Stop the person cannot send or regenerate until the server reaches its next completed line: a second or so with the fast stand-in, the whole thinking phase with a real model (often 10 to 30 seconds), and the whole call with Groq, which answers in one piece. During that time the model call keeps running and is paid for, and every attempt is refused with 'Wait for the current answer to finish.', which also uses up one of the five requests a minute (srv-05). A Groq answer whose client left is stored as 'stopped' with every line but the last. If the PHP worker is killed mid-answer (deploy restart, out of memory) the finally block never runs and the person is locked out of Ask AI for the full 150 seconds.
fix: Make the abort probe write. In AskAiController::chat() keep $lastWrite = microtime(true), set it in writeEvent(), and pass as $aborted: function () use (&$lastWrite): bool { if (microtime(true) - $lastWrite >= 2.0) { echo ": keep-alive\n\n"; if (ob_get_level() > 0) { @ob_flush(); } flush(); $lastWrite = microtime(true); } return connection_aborted() === 1; }. The contract already allows the comment line and the client parser skips it. In $onEvent also call $aborted() inside the line loop before each $release($line). Shorten the lock to the real ceiling (answer deadline 75 s plus Groq's 12 s plus a margin, about 100 s). Test: a fake generator that sends only reasoning text with no newline for several events, with an $aborted probe that turns true after the first call, must end in ChatInterrupted before any text is released.

title: The chat route now shares the 5-per-minute 'ai-generation' bucket, so the sixth message in a minute is refused, greetings included
evidence: Route::post('/ai/assistant/chat', ...)->middleware(['throttle:ai-generation', ...]) with AppServiceProvider line 168: RateLimiter::for('ai-generation', fn (Request $request) => Limit::perMinute(5)->by($authenticatedKey($request))...). The same limiter and key serve /announcements/generate-draft, /events/{id}/generate-plan, /budgets/{id}/advice, /forecasts/generate and the two new action routes (lines 118-119). Live on :8000 as student 2100142: five 'hello' messages answered, the sixth -> HTTP 429 {"message":"Too many requests. Please wait before trying again."}. Contract section 2 says writes use throttle:api-write.
impact: A conversation is short turns. Greetings, thanks, memory commands, Try again, Regenerate and requests refused by the per-user lock all count, so a person who asks five quick things is told to wait a minute, and an Admin who has been chatting cannot generate an event plan or a budget advice (and the reverse). Cancelling an action card also spends from the same five.
fix: Give chat its own limiter now that one answer at a time per user is enforced by the lock: in AppServiceProvider add RateLimiter::for('ai-chat', fn (Request $request) => Limit::perMinute(20)->by('chat:'.$authenticatedKey($request))->response($tooManyRequests)); and use 'throttle:ai-chat' on /ai/assistant/chat. Put action/confirm and action/cancel on 'throttle:api-write' (they call no model). Update contract section 2 to name the chat limiter. Test: six chat messages in a row are all answered, and a chat message does not reduce what /announcements/generate-draft has left.

title: The model is told the active semester while the records are read for the semester the person has selected
evidence: chatContext(): $semester = AcademicSemester::active(); ... 'semester' => ... 'AY '.$semester->academicYear->label.' · '.$this->semesterLabel(...). The builders the same request runs use AcademicSemester::selected() (for example SemesterScope::budgets($budgets, AcademicSemester::selected()) and the elections, events and fee queries), and the client sends X-Academic-Semester on the chat request. Checked on an in-memory database with semester 1 closed and semester 2 active and the header set to semester 1: AcademicSemester::selected() returns semester 1 (closed) while chatContext() returns "AY 2026-2027 · 2nd Semester".
impact: An Admin, officer, Department Head or the SAO who has the period switcher on an earlier semester gets that semester's budgets, events and elections described as the current one ('this semester you have ...', 'in the 2nd Semester ...'). The figures are real but attached to the wrong period, and the number check cannot catch it.
fix: In chatContext() use AcademicSemester::selected() for the label, and when its id differs from AcademicSemester::active()?->id append ' (not the current semester)' so the model says which period it is describing. Change contract 6.2 from 'the active semester label' to 'the label of the semester the request works in'. Test: with the header naming a closed semester, the facts in AskAiChatFakeGenerator::lastUserTurn() carry that semester's label.

title: Regenerate erases an action card that was already carried out and offers the same action again
evidence: respond(): $conversation->messages()->reorder()->where('role', 'assistant')->where('id', '>', $userMessage->id)->get()->each(fn (AiMessage $replaced) => $replaced->eraseWithOutput()); then line 105 runs $this->actions->propose(...) again for the same typed message. Nothing looks at payload.action.status. Run against the current code: 'I want to create an event called General Assembly' -> card create_event, awaiting_confirmation; set the card to status done (what AskAiActionController::confirm stores after it creates the event); regenerate -> the done card no longer exists and a new card with status awaiting_confirmation is returned.
impact: After an event, task, budget proposal, announcement draft or grievance has been created from the chat, a regenerate request removes the only record in the conversation that it was done and returns a fresh card for the same request; pressing its button creates the record a second time. Regenerating while a confirm is in flight (status confirming) deletes the row the confirm request is about to update, so that request fails after the action ran.
fix: In assertRegenerable() (so the 422 is sent before a stream starts) load the assistant messages after the last user message and refuse when any has payload.action.status in ['done', 'confirming']: throw ValidationException::withMessages(['regenerate' => 'That request was already carried out. Ask again to start a new one.']). Keep allowing regenerate for awaiting_confirmation, cancelled, expired and failed cards. Add a test for the done and the confirming case, and state the rule in the actions contract.

title: The model's thinking now reaches the client after the answer instead of as it arrives
evidence: if ($type === 'reasoning') { $reasoningPending .= $delta; while (($position = strpos($reasoningPending, "\n")) !== false) { $keepReasoning(...); ... } return; }  and only after converse() returns (line 418): if (trim($reasoningPending) !== '') { $keepReasoning($reasoningPending); }. A thinking summary is usually one paragraph with no newline. Live on :8002 the event order is now: meta, status, status, status, delta x9, reasoning, delta, done. Before this change the same stream sent eight reasoning events before the first delta.
impact: Contract section 5 says the reasoning event carries the thinking summary as it arrives, and the page shows it while the person waits. Now the panel stays empty for the whole thinking phase and the text appears when the answer is already complete, so the wait looks like a hang. It also removes the writes that used to let the server notice a stop during thinking (srv-04).
fix: Release thinking by sentence as well as by line, and flush it when writing starts. In the reasoning branch, after the newline loop, release complete sentences: while (preg_match('/^(.+?[.!?])\s+(.*)$/su', $reasoningPending, $m) === 1) { $keepReasoning($m[1]); $reasoningPending = $m[2]; }. At the top of the text branch add: if (trim($reasoningPending) !== '') { $keepReasoning($reasoningPending); } $reasoningPending = '';. keepReasoning() joins pieces with a newline, so join sentence pieces with a space instead when the piece did not follow a newline. Extend test_the_stream_emits_meta_status_delta_and_done... to assert that the reasoning event comes before the first delta when the fake's reasoning has no newline.

title: The shipped nginx and php-fpm settings are not sized for a stream that can stay open 75 seconds
evidence: location = /index.php { ... include fastcgi_params; fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME ...; fastcgi_pass unix:/run/php/php8.3-fpm.sock; } with no fastcgi_read_timeout, so nginx's default of 60 seconds between two reads applies. AskAiChatService::answerSeconds() allows chat_timeout (60) + 15 = 75 seconds, the Claude call may run its full 60 seconds and Groq then up to 12 more, and the server never sends the ': keep-alive' comment the contract allows. scripts/server/php holds only 20-hiusa.ini (upload sizes); nothing in the repository sets pm.max_children, and each open chat occupies one php-fpm worker until its answer ends.
impact: When the first provider stalls and the second answers (the case the fallback exists for), no byte is sent for more than 60 seconds, nginx closes the connection, the page shows 'Could not answer that right now', and the answer that then arrives is stored as 'stopped' and replaced by the retry. Separately, with the packaged php-fpm default of 5 workers, five people waiting on answers at the same moment leave no worker for sign-in, payments or voting until one finishes. The pool size on the live server must be checked; the repository does not set it.
fix: In scripts/server/nginx/hiusa.conf add to the index.php location: fastcgi_read_timeout 120s; (longer than the 75 s answer ceiling plus Groq's 12 s). Send the keep-alive comment from the abort probe as described in srv-04. Add scripts/server/php/hiusa-pool.conf (or document in LIGHTSAIL_DEPLOYMENT_AND_MAINTENANCE.md) a pool sized for the instance, for example pm = dynamic, pm.max_children = 20, pm.start_servers = 4, pm.min_spare_servers = 2, pm.max_spare_servers = 6, and have deploy-lightsail.sh install it; confirm the value on the server before release.

title: Regenerate deletes the audit row of the answer it replaces, and action cards write no audit row
evidence: ->each(fn (AiMessage $replaced) => $replaced->eraseWithOutput());  AiMessage::eraseWithOutput() deletes the message and AiOutput::query()->whereKey($outputId)->delete(). AskAiActions::propose() creates the assistant message with no AiOutput and no ai_output_id. Contract section 1: 'Every assistant answer still writes one ai_outputs row ... (the audit trail and ai:live-eval rely on it)'.
impact: Deleting a conversation removing its ai_outputs rows was a privacy decision and is right. Regenerate is not a request to delete anything, yet the answer the person rejected (often the one they marked thumbs-down) disappears from the audit trail, so the trail no longer shows what the assistant actually said. Answers that propose an action leave no ASK_AI_ASSISTANT row at all.
fix: On regenerate call $replaced->delete() and keep the ai_outputs row (the foreign key nulls nothing because the message is the referencing side). So that deleting the conversation later still removes it, make AiConversation::eraseWithOutputs() also delete AiOutput rows where feature_type = 'ASK_AI_ASSISTANT' and structured_input->conversation_id is in the ids (storeAnswer already writes conversation_id there). Write an ai_outputs row for an action proposal, or state in both contracts that proposals are not audited there. Update contract section 1 with the deletion rule.

title: The reasoning steps and notices describe work that did not happen
evidence: finishDeterministic(): $steps[] = $why === 'guard' ? 'Found a figure ...' : 'Wrote the answer directly from your records'; steps() line 805 falls back to 'Looked through the records your account can open'; finishModel() line 515: 'Stopped writing when you asked; kept the checked part'; line 449: $emit('replace', ['text' => $deterministicText, 'notice' => null]) when the provider fails after text was released. Run as a student asking 'show pending approvals': content 'A student account does not have access to approval queues ...' with steps ['Understood this as a question about pending approvals', 'Looked through the records your account can open', 'Wrote the answer directly from your records'].
impact: Contract 6.7 says the steps are built from what the server actually did. A refusal claims records were read and the answer written from them; a connection that dropped is recorded as the person asking to stop; and when the provider dies mid-answer the half-written text is swapped for a different one with no sentence explaining why.
fix: In answerFromRecords() pass a reason to finishDeterministic(): 'refused' when ! $allowedModel and the payload has no rag_metadata (steps: the 'Understood ...' line plus 'This is outside what your account can open, so no records were read'), 'provider' when $allowedModel and $result === null (step 'The writing service did not finish, so this is the summary from your records', and send that sentence as the notice of the replace event when text had been released). Word the stopped step neutrally: 'Writing stopped before the end; kept the checked part'.

title: The conversation list reads every row's full payload, the detail returns every message, and conversations past the newest 50 cannot be reached
evidence: scopeWithSummary(): 'preview_payload' => AiMessage::select('payload')->whereColumn(...)->where('role', 'assistant')->orderByDesc('id')->limit(1) is used only to read payload.intent; storeAnswer() stores every section row in the payload ('sections' => $payloadBase['sections'], uncapped). AskAiController::conversations(): ->limit(50)->get() with no offset or cursor; showConversation(): $row->messages()->get().
impact: Every list call and every search keystroke pulls up to 50 complete payloads (sections, rows, charts) out of the database to read one word each. A long conversation is returned whole, payloads included. A person with more than 50 conversations can only find the older ones by searching for a word they remember; nothing lists them.
fix: Select only the intent: 'preview_intent' => AiMessage::select('payload->intent')->... (Laravel writes the JSON path for MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite) and read that in conversationRow(). Add ?before=<id> to the list (where('id', '<', $before), same order, 50 rows, plus has_more) and to the detail (latest 100 messages, older on request), and add both to contract section 2.

title: Tests cover the happy path of follow-ups, local commands and regenerate, not the cases that go wrong
evidence: test_a_new_subject_is_not_forced_onto_the_previous_intent uses 'How is our budget doing this semester', which the keyword classifier already routes, so it never reaches looksLikeFollowUp(). test_regenerate_answers_the_last_question_when_no_answer_follows_it (line 749) has one question and no earlier answer. No test sends a memory or capabilities phrase inside a real question, a number that exists only in history or memory, or more than five messages in a minute. The 52 tests in AskAiChatTest and AskAiChatScopeTest pass while srv-01, srv-02, srv-03 and srv-05 are all reproducible.
impact: The stream test does read the stream (streamedContent() runs the callback and the events are parsed), and the scope tests do prove the privacy rule for another user, a role change and an organization change, including what reaches the model. But the suite gives no warning for the defects above, and a later change to regenerate could delete the previous turn's answer without failing a test.
fix: Add: (1) regenerate with messages [question 1, answer 1, question 2] keeps answer 1, answers question 2 and leaves three then four rows; (2) the follow-up, local-command and number tests listed in srv-01 to srv-03; (3) a request-level test that six chat messages in a minute are answered once srv-05 is fixed; (4) a stream test where the fake's reasoning has no newline and the reasoning event must precede the first delta (srv-08).
